Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

think verb

ponder, think about

also think about, think of, reflect, ponder, think something over, think over

classical

Sen. Ep. 63.2: etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse
Cic. Off. 1.105: mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

cōgitō, cōgitāre, cōgitāvī, cōgitātum

verb, first conjugation

think (about), ponder

With dē and the ablative for what one thinks about (dē tē cōgitō), an accusative, or a question (quid agam cōgitō). With an infinitive it means “intend” (see mean, intend).

Other words

  • reputō, reputāre, reputāvī, reputātum — think over, reflect on

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 591: Dum haec mēcum reputō; Traupman 109: aliquid sēcum reputāre; Traupman 393

    Mostly with sēcum or cum animō: turning something over in one’s mind.

Examples

  • aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet, cōnserere cōgitāre nōn oportet, sed facere oportet

    Building you should think about for a long time; planting you shouldn’t think about: you should just do it.Cato, Agr. 3.1

  • cum dīxerit etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse

    since Homer said that even Niobe thought about foodSen. Ep. 63.2

See also think, mind, mean, consider.
